info.title: UARP — Universal Agent Runtime Platform
info.description:
API for managing AI agents, runs, sessions, and supporting infrastructure.

Auth: bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer uarp_<prefix>_<secret>`). Browser SSE/WebSocket clients that cannot set headers may pass the same key as `?token=<api_key>` query param or `uarp_auth_token` cookie.

Idempotency: every AUTHENTICATED mutating `/api/v1/*` request accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header; replays within 24 h return the cached response with `X-Idempotency-Replayed: true`. Anonymous operations — inbound webhooks, sign-in exchanges (`/register`, `/auth/*`), `/public/*` session calls — carry no caller identity to key on and do not take it; the header is declared only on the operations that honour it.

Versioning: `X-API-Version` is a RESPONSE header — the contract date the server runs (`2026-09-10`), bumped only on a breaking change. A request header of the same name is not read: there is no version negotiation, so pinning an older date does not keep an older behaviour (measured 2026-09-10: `2025-03-01`, `2020-01-01` and `garbage` all answer identically). `X-API-Deprecation-Info` is always `none` today; `Deprecation`/`Sunset` (RFC 8594) exist in the middleware and are not yet emitted for any operation.

Field form: snake_case. The camelCase fields still on the wire are each marked `deprecated` beside their snake_case twin — both spellings carry the same value for a compatibility window that closes in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`); read the snake_case one. `applinks.details[].appIDs` in the Apple app-site-association document is Apple's format, not ours.

Scopes: each operation names the key scope it requires in `x-scopes`; the catalogue with descriptions is `x-scopes` on the `bearerAuth` scheme. The `security` block stays `[{bearerAuth: []}]` because OpenAPI reads scope strings only on an `oauth2` scheme and these are API keys.

Bounds: a string or array in a request body is bounded by the body cap the server enforces (10 MiB for a JSON document, 50 MiB on an upload route; 413 above) and the document says so as `maxLength`/`maxItems` unless a field states a tighter bound; a query, path or header parameter is bounded by the 64 KiB request line the edge accepts (the connection is closed above it, measured 2026-09-16). An integer's bound is whatever the handler validates or clamps, declared per field. Response fields carry no bound the server does not enforce.

x-scopes.admin: Platform administration: `/admin/*` configuration, providers, tenants, the Stripe DLQ. Most of these operations additionally require role `admin` or the super-admin (an RBAC layer beyond scope).
x-scopes.agents:read: Read agents, their versions, activity and system cards; teams, programs, companies and the LLM catalogue.
x-scopes.agents:write: Create, update, delete and configure agents, teams, programs, companies, integrations and schedules.
x-scopes.analytics:read: Read the analytics overview and usage breakdowns. This is the resource:action spelling every other scope uses; the pre-2026-09-10 name `read:analytics` is still accepted as an alias (analytics.ts) — measured 2026-09-10 on production: no issued key carries either spelling, the four analytics routes are reached through `*` keys — and is removed on a date the owner names.
x-scopes.api_keys:read: List the tenant's API keys and read the tenant record.
x-scopes.billing:read: Read plans, usage, quota, invoices, the budget and overage settings.
x-scopes.billing:write: Change the plan, budget, overage and promo codes; open the Stripe portal.
x-scopes.drawing:read: Read a session's drawing: the document, the op journal, renders, tiles and masks.
x-scopes.drawing:write: Append ops to a session's drawing, make masks and delete drawings.
x-scopes.evaluations:read: Read evaluation suites and their results.
x-scopes.events:read: Subscribe to run, session and team event streams (SSE and WebSocket).
x-scopes.files:read: Read and download files and workspace contents.
x-scopes.files:write: Upload, change and delete files and workspace contents.
x-scopes.marketplace:write: Publish, update and withdraw marketplace listings.
x-scopes.memory:read: Read agent memory and knowledge bases.
x-scopes.memory:write: Write agent memory and knowledge-base documents.
x-scopes.notifications:read: Read notifications and the unread count.
x-scopes.notifications:write: Mark, dismiss and configure notifications and push subscriptions.
x-scopes.runs:create: Start runs, chat completions, responses and embeddings.
x-scopes.runs:read: Read runs, their events, artifacts, replays and the feed.
x-scopes.sessions:read: Read sessions, messages, todos, projects and drawings.
x-scopes.sessions:write: Create and change sessions, messages, todos, projects, annotations and feedback.
x-scopes.tenants:write: Change the tenant and its settings.
x-scopes.users:write: Invite, change and remove users; manage roles and MFA.
x-scopes.webhooks:write: Create, update, delete and test webhooks.

bearerAuth.description:
API key in `Authorization: Bearer uarp_<prefix8>_<secret32>` header.

Scopes: the catalogue is `x-scopes` on this scheme (`{scope: description}`), and each operation names the scope it requires in its own `x-scopes` array — the `security` block of an operation stays `[{bearerAuth: []}]` because the OpenAPI specification reads scope strings only on an `oauth2` scheme, and these are API keys, not OAuth. An operation without `x-scopes` accepts any authenticated key; an empty `security: []` marks an anonymous operation. Keys carry scopes as issued (`*` grants everything); `requireScope` in the route handlers is what enforces them. Most `/admin/*` endpoints additionally require role `admin` (RBAC layer beyond scope).

queryTokenAuth.name: token
queryTokenAuth.description: Same API key passed via `?token=<uarp_<prefix>_<secret>>` query param. Used for SSE/WebSocket/file content endpoints that cannot set request headers from a browser. For `/runs/{runId}/events` and `/sessions/{sessionId}/events` the recommended flow is to mint a short-lived token via `POST /api/v1/auth/sse-tokens` (60 s TTL, scope-restricted).

cookieAuth.name: uarp_auth_token
cookieAuth.description: Same API key set as a cookie. Used by the builder web app and any HTML rendering endpoint behind same-origin auth.

webSocketProtocolAuth.name: Sec-WebSocket-Protocol
webSocketProtocolAuth.description: WebSocket upgrade only: subprotocol of the form `uarp.<base64(api_key)>`. Used by `/api/v1/bridge/ws` and other WebSocket upgrade routes.

DropGenome.description: The mascot character of an agent (DropGenome in @uarp/runtime): silhouette, motion and affect parameters plus a signature pose. Written by the platform at create/backfill or by a client from the builder.

AgentMetadataUi.description: The `metadata.ui` record three clients and the platform share. PATCH merges it one level, and `avatar` one level deeper: a client that sends `{protocol, variant}` keeps the stored `hue`, one that sends `{hue}` keeps `protocol` and `variant` (agent-genome.ts mergeAgentMetadata; owner 2026-09-10).

avatar.description: Identity: which drawing protocol, which variant, and the hue (degrees). Merged field by field on PATCH.

drop_genome_source.description: Provenance of the FIRST server-written genome — set only by the platform (ensureAgentGenome / the create path), never by a client, and left untouched by client PATCHes of `drop_genome`. Absent when the genome was client-authored or predates the field.

ReadinessReport.description: GET /health/ready and GET /readyz (measured 2026-09-10): overall status, the check's timestamp, and one entry per component — cron, events, kv, mcp, workers.

FileRecord.description: A stored file as GET /files/{fileId} serves it (measured 2026-09-10 on e2e-canon). POST /files returns the same record plus `url`.

TeamRunDetail.description: GET /teams/{teamId}/runs/{teamRunId} and GET /squads/{squadId}/runs/{teamRunId} (measured 2026-09-10 on e2e-canon, identical on both routes): the team run and the member runs it spawned.

PlaygroundAgentState.description: The visual-builder canvas of an agent as GET /playground/agents/{agentId} serves it (measured 2026-09-10 on e2e-canon); PUT returns the same shape after the write.

PlaygroundTemplate.description: One starter template from GET /playground/templates (element keys measured 2026-09-10).

DeadlockReport.description: governance/emergency.ts DeadlockReport — computed, not stored. Field names are camelCase on the wire.

hasDeadlock.description: Deprecated spelling of `has_deadlock` — the same value, kept for the compatibility window and removed in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`). Read `has_deadlock`.

conflictingRules.description: Deprecated spelling of `conflicting_rules` — the same value, kept for the compatibility window and removed in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`). Read `conflicting_rules`.

RootAttestation.description: governance/emergency.ts RootAttestation — the KV record, unsanitized.

SubjectSweep.description: What the scan actually looked at, on every access and erasure answer. A count of zero is otherwise unreadable: until 2026-09-16 every one of these counts was zero on every request ever made, and the reason was the matcher rather than the data.

identifiers_matched.description: How many identifiers the subject was matched on — the subject id plus the id of every api-key credential that acted for them. Never the identifiers themselves: a key id is a credential reference and this payload goes to the requester.

prefixes_scanned.description: KV prefixes walked to exhaustion in this tenant.

fields_matched.description: Record fields compared against the identifier set.

no_records_matched.description: True when nothing matched, so a zero can be read as a zero.

DataSubjectAccessReport.description: data-subject.ts dataSubjectAccess — ids per store plus their counts; every field always present.

core_memory.description: Core-memory labels, when the subject is an agent. A human subject has no core-memory rows of their own.

not_exported.description: What this endpoint does NOT return, named rather than left to be assumed: the record CONTENTS (each list is identifiers, to be fetched through the per-record routes), and the families that carry no subject identifier at all — knowledge-base documents and workspace files.

DataSubjectErasureResult.description: data-subject.ts dataSubjectErasure — `erased` plus the SubjectErasureCounts spread.

not_erased.description: Record families this sweep did not touch, and why. Knowledge-base documents and workspace files carry no subject identifier of any kind, so there is nothing to match a subject on and no honest way to erase theirs without erasing everyone's — the caller is told, with the route to do it by hand.

PublicAgentCard.description: public.ts GET /public/agents/{agentId} — a hand-built projection, not the Agent record. Keys whose value is undefined are dropped from the JSON, so everything but `agent_id`, `name` and `icon` is conditional; `specs` is omitted entirely when empty.

capabilities.description: `"N tools available"`, only when `public_config.allowed_tools` is set.

tenant_slug.description: The tenant that owns the agent — the same value as `PublicTenant.slug`. The `/c/{slug}/{agentId}` path segment is NOT authoritative (nothing checks it against the agent); compare it with this and build the way back from here. Present when the owner record has a slug.

tenant_name.description: The owning tenant's display name. Present when the owner record has one.

PublicSessionView.description: public.ts GET /public/sessions/{sessionId} — every field always present; compacted entries are filtered out and non-string content is JSON-stringified.

message_id.description: The same derived id the authenticated transcript carries (ConversationEntry.message_id).

OpenAiChatCompletion.description: An OpenAI Chat Completions object. `/v1/chat/completions` builds it (openai-compat.ts: exactly one choice, no `logprobs`, no `system_fingerprint`); `/api/v1/llm/chat/completions` passes the provider's body through (llm-proxy.ts) — `model` is then the provider's id, and a reasoning-only reply has its reasoning copied into `content`.

MarketplaceSubscription.description: marketplace/listing-store.ts MarketplaceSubscription — on subscribe, `status` is `active`, `stripe_subscription_id` is always present (the route rejects a body without it) and `created_at` equals `updated_at`.

stripe_subscription_id.description: The Stripe subscription (`sub_…`) the tenant pays through. Written by the bootstrap path and — since 2026-09-11 — by the subscription webhook (created/updated); cleared when the subscription is deleted. Absent while the tenant has none, and on tenants whose subscription arrived before the webhook stored it.

SessionAnnotation.description: sessions.ts AnnotationRecord — the six-field projection create, list and PATCH all answer with.

A2AAgentCard.description: a2a/agent-card.ts A2AAgentCard, built by buildAgentCard. `provider` is declared on the type and never emitted.

UsageQuota.description: billing.ts GET /usage/quota. `reason` only when `allowed` is false (billing/usage-tracker.ts checkQuota).

usage.description: billing/usage-tracker.ts AggregatedUsage for the current month.

source.description: Which layer is in force, decided by the stored HOST alone: a saved host makes it `kv`, otherwise an environment host makes it `env`, otherwise `none`. Note the consequence — saving a user or a password WITHOUT a host leaves `source` at `env` and the stored fields inert.

missing_required.description: Setup steps still outstanding. Non-empty means an attempt to open registration is refused, and this is the list it will name.

waitlist_count.description: How many tenants are waitlisted — ALL of them, counted by walking every KV page. It used to be `waitlist.length`, from a single unpaginated read, so past a thousand signups the number froze at exactly 1000 with nothing saying it had been cut (ADM-04). This is the number an admin uses to decide when to open registration, so it is the one that must be complete rather than the roster.

waitlist_truncated.description: True when `waitlist` holds fewer rows than `waitlist_count`. The roster is a display list and stays bounded at 1000; the count is not.

waitlist.description: Oldest first. Bounded at 1000 rows — check `waitlist_truncated` rather than taking `waitlist.length` as the total.

ResponsesOutputItem.description: openai-responses.ts — always exactly one message with one output_text part.

PendingApproval.description: runs.ts — the tool calls of the newest run.awaiting_approval event (agent-runtime.ts / bridge.ts); `options`/`kind` only from the bridge.

options.description: Choices the bridge reported for the approval, when any.

TeamRunChatTurn.description: teams.ts — the chat turn of a team run; at most one element.

CompanyActivityEntry.description: companies.ts — a company_activity row; `success` only when recorded.

MfaEnrolment.description: POST /auth/mfa/enrol (mfa.ts): the TOTP secret, its otpauth URL and the one-time recovery codes — shown once.

AuditLogEntry.description: One audit-log row as served by GET /runs/{runId}/audit-log and GET /sessions/{sessionId}/audit-log. Keys measured 2026-09-10 on the e2e-canon tenant (runs and sessions alike).

AgentCapabilities.description: What GET /agents/{agentId}/capabilities serves. Measured 2026-09-10 on the e2e-canon tenant; `tools[]` and `kb_ids[]` were empty there, so their element shape is not asserted.

RunFeedbackList.description: GET …/feedback without `message_id`: every reaction the caller stored on the run (measured 2026-09-10: `{"feedbacks":[]}` on a run with none).

message_id.description: The entry's `message_id` from GET /sessions/{sessionId}/messages (ConversationEntry.message_id) — the canonical key; any string is stored as sent.

reason.description: Present only when the reader gave one with the reaction.

RunFeedbackOne.description: GET …/feedback with `message_id`: that one reaction, `null` when the caller has not reacted.

reason.description: Present only when the reader gave one with the reaction.

RunFeedbackSet.description: PUT …/feedback: the stored reaction, echoed (runs.ts putRunFeedback, sessions.ts putSessionFeedback — the same literal).

reason.description: Echoed only when the caller sent one.

AgentBookmark.description: A message pinned under an agent. Keyed by `message_id`; the platform keeps the text the client sent, it does not look the message up.

WorkspaceFileVersion.description: One kept version of a workspace file. Keys as served 2026-09-10.

NotificationChannel.description: Delivery channel. `in_app` is always-on (bell drawer + SSE) and cannot be opted out of; `telegram`/`whatsapp` are reserved and have no adapter yet.

NotificationType.description: Fine-grained event type. There are no coarse buckets on the server — a UI that groups events (e.g. "agents / failures / system") maps its groups onto these types itself.

NotificationPreferencesInput.description: Per-TENANT notification routing. Sent to PUT /notifications/prefs, which REPLACES the stored value — an omitted field is stored as omitted (that is how a client clears `muted_types` or drops `quiet_hours`). `tenant_id` and `updated_at` are ignored if sent: the server derives them.

priority_channels.description: Default channel routing keyed by severity. Server default: critical → [in_app, email]; warning/info/success → [in_app].

type_overrides.description: Per-event-type channel list. When present for a type it REPLACES the priority-level default for that type. Keys are NotificationType values.

muted_types.description: Event types muted for OUTBOUND delivery (email/webhook/push). The in-app bell still receives them — muting does not hide an event from the bell drawer, it only stops the outbound channels.

quiet_hours.description: Window during which non-critical messages are suppressed; critical always bypasses. Set both start_local and end_local to enable, empty disables.

timezone.description: IANA timezone (e.g. "Europe/Kyiv"). Defaults to UTC when absent.

allOf.description: The stored value as returned by GET/PUT — same shape plus the server-derived fields.

Error.description: RFC 9457 problem document; `correlation_id` (the request id, echoed from `X-Request-Id`) for tracing — `correlationId` is the same value for the compatibility window.

title.description: The HTTP reason phrase of `status` — one dictionary for every status the platform answers with (lib/error-titles.ts; the enum is built from it). The one deliberate exception: 422 says "Validation Error", as it always has. Never an exception class name; that lives in `code`.

detail.description: The sentence a person reads — specific to this occurrence, never empty, never a repeat of `title`. On a 500 it is the fixed sentence the sanitizer allows; 501–504 carry the handler's own operator guidance.

code.description: What a client should DO about this, as a value it can switch on — `detail` is for the person reading. The enum is built from the one dictionary in `types/error-codes.ts`, so the document and the wire cannot drift apart. Two casings are on the wire and both are load-bearing: SCREAMING_SNAKE came from the `UarpError` hierarchy, lower_snake from the hand-written limit refusals, and clients match on each exactly. Absent when the refusal has no machine-readable class.

correlationId.description: Request ID for tracing Deprecated spelling of `correlation_id` — the same value, kept for the compatibility window and removed in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`). Read `correlation_id`.

OpenAiError.description: Error envelope used by the OpenAI-compatible surface (`/v1/*`). Deliberately NOT RFC 9457: callers here are OpenAI SDKs pointed at this base URL, and they decode this shape.

message.description: Human-readable cause, including where an operator fixes it.

code.description: Machine-readable code. `embedding_unavailable` = no provider configured (501, permanent). `embedding_failed` = the configured provider did not answer (503, retryable).

mission.description: What the company exists to do.

budget.description: Spend ceiling and pacing for the company.

spent_usd.description: Metered by the platform. Ignored on create (set to 0) and on update.

CompanyUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/companies/{companyId}`. Every field optional — send only what changes.

workers.description: Each entry REQUIRES `agent_id` — omitting it answers `422 workers.0.agent_id: Required`.

TeamUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/teams/{teamId}`. Every field optional — send only what changes.

AgentUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /api/v1/agents/{agentId}`. Every field optional — an omitted field means NO CHANGE, not 'clear it'. `model` and `fallback_model` are accepted and ignored (see the model lockdown).

specs.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list; it is not merged. A PATCH carrying one id leaves the agent with exactly that one — read the current value and send the full set. The incoming list is normalised and persisted whole; the previous list is consulted only to keep permission-grant timestamps stable for SPECs that were already installed.

approval_required_tools.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list; it is not merged. A PATCH carrying one id leaves the agent with exactly that one — read the current value and send the full set.

auto_approve_tools.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list; it is not merged. A PATCH carrying one id leaves the agent with exactly that one — read the current value and send the full set.

knowledge_base_ids.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list; it is not merged. A PATCH carrying one id leaves the agent with exactly that one — read the current value and send the full set. Note the legacy singular `knowledge_base_id` is UNIONED with this array within the same request — the server-side helper is named `mergeKbIds` for that reason, and merges the two REQUEST fields, never the request with what is stored.

public_config.description: Partial: the handler merges it one level over the stored `public_config` (agents.ts, `{ ...existing.public_config, ...body.public_config }`), so `{ public_config: { enabled: true } }` flips the switch and keeps the greeting, limits and allowed tools. Sending `enabled` alone does not make the agent reachable — see `Agent.visibility`.

embedding_model.description: Informational only — not a choice. The deployment has one embedding model, set by the super-admin in `PUT /admin/config/agent-memory`; ingest and search always use it, and `POST /knowledge-bases/{id}/reindex` overwrites this field with the model actually used. A string sent here is stored and echoed by GET until the first reindex, then replaced. `PUT /knowledge-bases/{id}` ignores it. Clients should send nothing (knowledge-bases.ts:395, :688).

DesignRequestCreate.description: Body for `POST /api/v1/governance/builder/requests`. What `DesignRequestSubmitSchema` requires: `agent_name` and `agent_description`, neither optional. `submitted_by` is NOT accepted from the body — it comes from the authenticated caller. The block carried no `required` at all until 2026-09-18.

enabled.description: One of the three switches that make the agent reachable without a key (public.ts loadPublicAgent): `visibility` must be `public`, this must be true, and `status` must be `active` (or absent). Any one of them alone does nothing visible.

daily_message_limit.description: Messages per UTC day per visitor identity (a hash of IP + anonymous visitor id). Enforced ONLY for the featured landing agent — the one `GET /admin/config/landing` names as `public_agent_id`; every other public agent keeps its per-session caps and ignores this. Over the cap the server answers 429 with `code: "DAILY_LIMIT"`. Unset means the platform default of 15.

tools.description: Tool names the SPEC registered into the local runtime.

error.description: Failure detail when `status` is `failed` — artifact 404, SHA mismatch, capability conflict.

agent_id.description: The agent this step runs. An entry without it is silently discarded.

label.description: Display name for the step; falls back to the agent's own name.

prompt.description: Per-step instruction. Carried through the SCHEDULE too — dropping it there made every scheduled run fall back to the bare label while the manual run honoured it.

specs.description: SPECs installed on this agent, with version pin and granted permissions.

enabled.description: Soft-disable. false keeps the install history but skips injection.

auto_approve_tools.description: Tools this agent may call without a human-in-the-loop prompt.

metadata.description: Free-form caller-supplied metadata; `ui` is the one key with a shared, documented shape.

approval_required_tools.description: Tool names requiring human approval before execution

built_in_tools.description: Built-in tool names enabled for this agent

knowledge_base_id.description: Deprecated in `packages/types/agent.ts:296`; kept for pre-migration records. Use `knowledge_base_ids`. Documenting only the singular is why a client reading this schema could link one base to an agent that supports several.

knowledge_base_ids.description: Every knowledge base linked to the agent. `search_kb` searches all of them by default.

visibility.description: Who can reach the agent. The publication screen is built on this field — but `public` alone does not open the agent to the world: the anonymous routes (`GET /public/agents/{agentId}`, public sessions) answer only when `visibility` is `public` AND `public_config.enabled` is true AND `status` is `active` (public.ts loadPublicAgent). A client that shows "anyone with the link can reach this agent" on `visibility` alone shows it a step too early. Measured 2026-09-10 on a real tenant: the one agent with both switches answered 200 without a key, every other `public` one 404.

status.description: Governance state, distinct from a run's status.

tool_overrides.description: Per-tool trust, overriding the agent's default approval policy.

bridge.description: Present only on `GET /agents/{id}`, and only for a bridge agent. Computed at read time from the machines currently registered, never stored on the record.

context_window_size.description:
Number of recent MESSAGES to keep — not a token budget, and read only when `context_strategy` is `sliding_window`. Default 20. Under any other strategy it is ignored entirely.

Said explicitly because the name reads like a token ceiling and was used as one: the Head Agent tier template set it to 65536/131072/262144 as if it capped context, and a client posted those values believing they sized the window. The window is the model's — see `model.capabilities.max_context_tokens` — and what bounds history per call is `resource_limits.max_tokens_per_run` together with the platform's history-budget ratio.

AgentModelConfig.description: Model capabilities. Deliberately carries no provider or model identifier — see the model lockdown.

capabilities.description: Feature flags the client may branch on (e.g. `vision`, `tool_calls`, `streaming`). Absent when the platform has published none.

AgentModelConfigInput.description: Accepted and IGNORED. The platform default is applied on create and preserved on update, so sending this changes nothing. Kept so existing clients do not start failing validation.

execution_mode.description: Absent for platform-dispatched cloud runs. `bridge` is written by the platform when a local agent takes the run (run-dispatch.ts, bridge.ts); `async` is only ever an echo of a client-supplied value and has never been stored on production (measured 2026-09-10 over 8605 run records: absent 7738, bridge 867, async 0).

output.description: Run output — the same object rides in run events and in a public session's stream (RunOutput). When a run is truncated by its step-budget cutoff (output.truncated === true) AND the platform has UARP_CONTINUATION_TOKEN_KEY configured, output.continuation_token carries an opaque HMAC-signed token that resumes the run via POST /runs/{id}/continue. With no key configured no token is minted and the field is absent; the token is an opaque string to every client.

team_run_id.description: Team run ID if part of a team execution

RunOutput.description: What the runtime writes as a run's `output` (agent-runtime.ts, the normal completion and the max-steps cutoff). Measured 2026-09-10 on production, 8 640 stored runs: `{ response }` 6 722; `{ response, search_sources }` 334; `{ response, output_truncated }` 23; `{ response, search_sources, output_truncated }` 3; `{ response, truncated, continuation_token }` 3; `{ response, truncated }` 2; `{}` 3. A bridge agent (execution_mode bridge) reports its own output — `{ response: "" }` is what it has been sending. Additional keys are possible from that path; the five below are the platform's own.

search_sources.description: URLs a real `web_search` tool call returned during this run — read back out of the tool results (`URL:` lines, response-postprocessing.ts extractSearchSources, deduplicated, at most 8), NOT out of the model's text. Present only when non-empty. Provenance is the point: a chat surface unfurls only these into preview cards, so a URL the model wrote from memory is never dressed up as a verified source. Witness: run 019faf2c… on tenant 019d9364… (2026-07-29) carries 8, the first on en.wikipedia.org.

output_truncated.description: The model stopped because it ran out of OUTPUT tokens (`finish_reason: length`), not because it was finished — the answer ends mid-sentence. Present only when true; the chat offers "Continue generating" on this flag alone. Distinct from `truncated` (step budget). 26 stored runs carry it.

truncated.description: The run hit its step budget (max_steps) before finishing. Present only when true.

continuation_token.description: Opaque HMAC-signed token minted with `truncated` when UARP_CONTINUATION_TOKEN_KEY is configured; resumes the run via POST /runs/{id}/continue.

pricing_confidence.description: How the cost was priced (measured 2026-09-10 on e2e-canon; billing/cost-estimator.ts).

opacity.description: An integer 0–255, like every channel value in a drawing (docs/DESIGNER-CANVAS.md §4.4).

source.description: Set when the layer was placed from a generated or uploaded image.

Drawing.description: A drawing a person and an agent share in real time (docs/DESIGNER-CANVAS.md §4.1). Pixels live in 256×256 tiles behind the journal; this record is the structure.

seq.description: The last journal entry applied to this drawing.

snapshot_seq.description: The seq up to which tiles are materialised; 0 until the first snapshot.

t.description: Milliseconds from the start of the stroke, across every part.

spacing.description: Percent of `size` between dabs; the client spaces the points, the renderer stamps every point it is given.

DrawingOp.description: One journal op (docs/DESIGNER-CANVAS.md §4.2), discriminated by `type`: stroke, erase, fill, place_image, layer_add, layer_remove, layer_update, layer_reorder, undo, redo. A stroke longer than 1 024 points is sent in parts that share `stroke_id`, count `part` from 0 and carry `continues: true` on every part but the last; `t` runs across the parts. `encoding` is required and is `json` in v1.

index.description: Values below 0 are clamped, not refused.

DrawingSelectionShape.description: A selection in canvas pixels: `rect` {x, y, w, h}, `ellipse` {cx, cy, rx, ry} or `lasso` {points[]}.

DrawingMask.description: What a person hands the agent (docs/DESIGNER-CANVAS.md §4.3): the selection as an L8 PNG of the drawing's size plus its bounding box.

file_id.description: The L8 PNG in the workspace; also served by `…/masks/{maskId}/content`.

fork_point_run_id.description: The run this branch forked after. Empty when the session had no runs yet.
Defaults to the session's most recent run.

parent_branch_id.description: Defaults to the session's active branch.

name.description: Defaults to `branch-<first 8 characters of the branch id>`.

RunApproveRequest.description: The body is optional and carries at most a `response` for the agent. An unknown field is REFUSED, not ignored: `{"approved": false}` sent here used to be stripped in silence while the endpoint approved anyway and answered `{"approved": true}`. To refuse a tool call, POST /runs/{runId}/reject.

response.description: Optional message passed back to the agent alongside the approval.

team_id.description: Team ID if session belongs to a team

queue_mode.description: How to handle concurrent runs in this session

model_override.description: Per-conversation model override (in-chat model switcher). When set, runs in this session resolve their LLM from this config instead of the agent's default. Absent → agent default.

ConversationEntry.description: One entry of a session transcript — what GET /sessions/{sessionId}/messages serves in both `messages` and `items` (types/session.ts ConversationEntry, enriched on read by sessions.ts with the run's metrics and cost). Measured 2026-09-10 on e2e-canon: a user turn carries role, content, run_id, timestamp, compacted, importance; an assistant turn adds tool_calls, thinking, run_metrics, cost_usd.

message_id.description: The stable id of this entry — derived on read (lib/message-ids.ts), never stored, so every transcript has it: the first user turn of a run is `{run_id}`, the first assistant reply `{run_id}-reply`, further replies `{run_id}-reply-2`…, a second human turn of the same run `{run_id}-user-2`… (lib/message-ids.ts:16-19), tool results `{run_id}-tool-N` and system entries `{run_id}-system-N` numbered from 1 (the first is `-tool-1`, never bare `-tool`). Counted per run over the whole history before compaction, so it does not move. This is the canonical `message_id` for reactions (PUT /runs/{runId}/feedback), bookmarks (/agents/{agentId}/bookmarks/{messageId}) and annotations (POST /sessions/{sessionId}/annotations); it is a safe path segment.

content.description: The text, or content parts for a multimodal turn (types/llm.ts MessageContent). v1 emits the string arm: every writer (renderUserTurn, SessionMessageSchema.content, ImportSessionMessageSchema) stores a string, and every stored entry on production is one (8 427 of 8 427, measured 2026-09-11). The array arm is the LLM wire type (types/llm.ts MessageContent) the schema inherits; a v2 server accepts only the string.

tool_calls.description: Persisted on assistant entries when the run executed tools. Reload re-paints these blocks underneath the assistant turn (matches what the SSE stream renders during the live run).

thinking.description: Reasoning / thinking content (DeepSeek `reasoning_content`, Anthropic extended thinking, GLM/Qwen `<think>` blocks). Persisted on assistant entries so reload re-paints the Thinking section above the assistant text.

run_metrics.description: On an assistant entry: the run's metrics as served by GET /runs/{runId} (sessions.ts publicRunMetrics).

cost_usd.description: On an assistant entry, when the run recorded a cost.

from_todo.description: The reply came from a run a Todo triggered.

output_truncated.description: The model ran out of output tokens — see RunOutput.output_truncated.

run_outcome.description: Present on entries written from a run (seen on some e2e-canon entries, absent on others).

AgentAnalyticsSummary.description: Output of summariseAgents (analytics.ts) — same shape for /admin/analytics/agents and /analytics/agents (tenant-scoped).

virtual.description: Present and `true` only when no document is stored and these are the genesis defaults computed on read; absent on a stored document (measured 2026-09-10).

rule.description: The new rule, for `add` and `modify`. Absent on `remove`.

approved_by.description: The founder, or the consensus that carried it.

scope.description: Who the rule binds. The document previously listed `global`/`tenant`/`agent`, none of which the server has ever emitted.

scope_targets.description: Agent ids, team ids or role names, depending on `scope`. Absent for `all_agents`.

action.description: The action the rule governs, e.g. `modify_constitution`.

obligated_action.description: For `requirement` rules: the action that must be performed.

immutable.description: Genesis rules cannot be amended or removed.

priority.description: Conflict resolution — higher wins. Defaults to 0.

advisory.description: True when no code path can ever raise this rule — the platform emits no such action (the constitution digest lists it under ADVISORY and boot logs "Constitution rules that can never fire"). A rulebook used to show these as enforced and LOCKED over an audit page with no such entries. Served since 2026-09-11; absent on older servers means unknown, not false.

allowed.description: False when any matched rule carries a blocking penalty.

checked_rules.description: Rule ids actually evaluated. Empty means no rule applied — never that nothing was checked.

checkResult.description: Deprecated spelling of `check_result` — the same value, kept for the compatibility window and removed in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`). Read `check_result`.

ruleId.description: Deprecated spelling of `rule_id` — the same value, kept for the compatibility window and removed in the next breaking release (the one that moves `X-API-Version`). Read `rule_id`.

penalties.description: What the matched rules call for. Empty when nothing matched.

checked_rules.description: Rule ids actually evaluated. Empty means no rule applied — never that nothing was checked.

seq.description: Position in the ONE global chain shared by all tenants — not a per-tenant sequence. Consecutive rows in a tenant's page usually have gaps here; the missing numbers are other tenants' entries (see the /governance/ledger description). For the tenant's own count use `tenant_total` on the list response.

prev_hash.description: Hash of the preceding entry. Null only for the genesis entry.

alignment_justification.description: How the goal squares with the constitution — written by the formulating agent.

proposal_id.description: Set once the goal reaches a vote. Absent before that.

UsageSummary.description: Tenant usage for one billing period. Flat — the counters are top-level, not nested under a `usage` object.

total_cost.description: What the tenant is billed, in USD.

provider_cost.description: What the upstream providers charged, in USD.

code.description: The value delivered in the callback fragment.

code_verifier.description: The secret whose SHA-256, base64url-encoded, was sent as `app_code_challenge` when the flow started. It never leaves the app, which is what makes an intercepted code worthless.

changelog.description: Free text when a client sent one with POST /agents/{agentId}/versions. The SERVER writes these fixed values of its own on the versions it mints — known values a client may match on, and therefore part of the contract (a test keeps this list equal to the literals in the code): `Initial version`, `Initial version (auto-created)`, `Initial version (created by agent factory)`, `Auto-versioned before update`, `Auto-versioned after update`, `Auto-versioned after update (retry)`, `Updated by agent factory`, `Head Agent orchestration kernel installed (agent-factory + discovery)`, `Head Agent orchestration kernel back-filled (agent-factory + discovery)`, `Rollback to version N` (N = the version rolled back to), `Self-improvement: N changes based on N analysis` (the self-improvement loop: the first N is a count, the second is one of errors, ratings or feedback — words, not a number). A reason code beside the prose is the owner's decision (DEC 11).

config.description: The full agent configuration as it stood at this version. Shape follows `Agent`; not pinned here so the two cannot drift.

seq.description: Global sequence of the newest ledger entry across ALL tenants — not the newest entry in the accompanying page. Measured 2026-08-20: `head.seq` was 6698 while the last visible entry was 6697, and the gap is another tenant's row. A client must not use this to decide whether it holds the latest page.

Invite.description: An invite as an administrator sees it. The accept token (`secret`) is NOT here: it travels in the email link and, for the recipient only, in `GET /me/tenants` `pending_invites`. Until 2026-09-12 the tenant's list, the 201, resend and revoke echoed it, so `users:read` could accept any pending invite of the tenant.

embedding_status.description: `embedded` when the document's chunks have vectors; `keyword_only` when no embedding provider answered and the document is searchable by keywords only.

excerpt.description: Body with its leading heading and markdown punctuation stripped, first 240 characters.

status.description: The MCP session status on success; the literal `error` when the probe failed.

mode.description: Which pass produced the results; null when the knowledge base is empty and neither ran.

source.description: Document label, sanitised before it is rendered into a prompt.

emailed.description: Whether a letter went out on THIS request. False when no testing URL is configured, when SMTP refused, when the address is inside its 24-hour resend cooldown, or when the platform-wide hourly send ceiling is reached. The address is recorded in every one of those cases — a "here is your link" letter without a link is worse than silence — so a client must NOT read `emailed: false` as "testing has not opened yet".

first_ip_hash.description: Truncated hash of the first submitting address. The raw IP is never stored.

emailed_at.description: `last_email_at` under the name the admin table renders; null rather than absent so a column can bind to it.

agent_name.description: Present only on the session-scoped list; absent from GET /todos.

messages.description: The conversation as it stood at this checkpoint — the model-facing ChatMessage list the runtime stores (checkpoint-manager.ts CheckpointData / continuation.ts); a manual checkpoint row carries none.

metrics.description: Accumulated run metrics — `RunMetricsAccumulator` (`runtime/core/step-executor.ts:156`): step and token counters, optionally provider cache hits.

default_model.description: Stored model half. May be bare (`minimax-m3`) or already provider-qualified (`ollama/glm-5.2`) — production holds both shapes. Dial `default_model_ref` instead of joining this yourself.

fallback_model.description: Stored model half of the fallback. A vendor path (`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`) carries a slash while naming no provider, so this string is NOT dialable on its own — use `fallback_model_ref`.

default_model_ref.description: The default as the chat surface accepts it: `provider/model`, already de-duplicated against a model half that carries the provider head. Null when no default model is configured.

fallback_model_ref.description: Same for the fallback. Null when no fallback model is configured.

first_invalid_seq.description: Sequence of the first entry that failed verification. Absent when `valid` is true.

VetoRecord.description: A veto as issued and listed (VetoRecord in @uarp/governance). Shape from the store's record; no tenant in reach had a veto to measure on 2026-09-10.

Ambassador.description: Keys as served by GET /governance/ambassador/ambassadors and …/{id} (measured 2026-09-10).

ScheduleEntry.description: What `PUT /agents/{agentId}/schedule` returns: the stored entry with its `config` nested (ScheduleEntry in @uarp/scheduler). `GET` returns the flattened `Schedule` instead.

next_fire_at.description: The next fire when `enabled` is true. On a disabled schedule the server keeps the last computed instant, so it can lie in the past (measured 2026-09-10 on two disabled entries).

status.description: State of the scheduler ENTRY (ScheduleEntry.status in @uarp/scheduler), not whether the schedule is switched on: measured 2026-09-10, `active` on every live entry, including two with `enabled: false`. The human-facing on/off is `enabled`.

Schedule.description: What `GET /agents/{agentId}/schedule` returns: `agent_id`, the config fields flattened, and the runtime state. Keys as served 2026-09-10; `last_fired_at`, `autonomous_mode` and `reflection_prompt` appear only when set.

status.description: State of the scheduler ENTRY (ScheduleEntry.status in @uarp/scheduler), not whether the schedule is switched on: measured 2026-09-10, `active` on every live entry, including two with `enabled: false`. The human-facing on/off is `enabled`.

next_fire_at.description: The next fire when `enabled` is true. On a disabled schedule the server keeps the last computed instant, so it can lie in the past (measured 2026-09-10 on two disabled entries).

ResourcePermission.description: Accepted, stored, and enforced by nothing (GOV-D01). The subset check that governs agent-to-agent spawn examines tools, roles, budget, spawn depth and self-modify, and never this field; no reader anywhere consults it to gate access to a resource. Granting or revoking it changes what an operator sees stored and nothing about what an agent may do. Documented rather than removed or enforced: removing it would break a field tenants may already have populated, and enforcing it would invent an authorisation rule the platform has never applied.

PermissionSetUpdate.description: Body of PUT /governance/permissions/{agentId}. Every field optional: a field the body omits keeps its stored value (mergePermissionSet), and only a first write falls back to the defaults. `agent_id`, `tenant_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` are set by the server and ignored in the body.

allowed_tools.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list (the handler stores the array as sent, it does not merge).

allowed_roles.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list (the handler stores the array as sent, it does not merge).

resource_permissions.description: Sending this field REPLACES the stored list (the handler stores the array as sent, it does not merge).

SpawnPolicyUpdate.description: Body of PUT /governance/permissions/spawn-policy. The handler requires the whole record (requireWholeRecord): all five fields, every time; `tenant_id` is the caller's and is not accepted in the body.

child_budget_ratio.description: Child agent gets at most this fraction of parent's budget.

allowed_roles.description: Whole-record write: the array is stored as sent, REPLACING the stored list.

PermissionSet.description: Per-agent capability envelope. Invariant: PermissionSet(child) ⊆ PermissionSet(parent).

chain.description: Full chain from root to this agent.

child_budget_ratio.description: Child agent gets at most this fraction of parent's budget.

revenue_error.description: Set when the run succeeded but the publisher payout failed — not a failed run.

DesignRequest.description: Governance-builder request to design a new agent (packages/governance/builder-flow.ts).

proposal_id.description: Set once the request enters a vote.

spawned_agent_id.description: Set once the approved design has been created.

ImprovementProposal.description: Self-improvement proposal — multi-stage state machine (proposed → arbiter_review → voting → sandbox_testing → approved → applied | rejected at any step).

version.description: Was declared `string` here while the record has always carried a number.

title.description: The proposal's heading. Undeclared until now, so a client built from this document rendered the card without one.

failed_run_ids.description: The failed runs that prompted the proposal.

changes.description: The proposed changes. Declared as `diff` here and stored as `changes`, so a client reading the documented name found nothing and showed "no diff" over a proposal that had one.

sandbox_success_rate.description: Present only after the sandbox stage has run.

vote_proposal_id.description: Set once the proposal reaches a vote.

files.description: Attachment ids the user added to this message. Fetch each with GET /files/{fileId}/content (scope files:read). Absent when the message had no attachment.

attachments.description: The attachments, in the same order as `files`, with what a client needs BEFORE it spends a fetch: a 40 MB video and a 2 KB note are not the same decision, and an error that cannot name the file leaves the model answering about a document it never opened. This is the SUBSET of `files` whose artifact record still exists when the task is enqueued — a run dispatched from a schedule was written earlier and the file may have been deleted since. An id present in `files` with no entry here means the file is gone, not that its metadata was omitted; fetching it will 404, which is how the client reports the attachment as not delivered.

BridgeTaskEvent.description: A progress frame from the Snaga bridge (BridgeTaskEvent in @uarp/types); `type` decides which optional fields are present.

TeamWorkerPermissions.description: What a worker may do inside a team run.

tools.description: Tool names this worker may invoke. Defaults to the agent's own allowed_tools.

TeamWorkerExternalA2A.description: Delegate this worker to another platform over the A2A protocol.

TeamWorker.description: An agent acting in a team, with a role and permissions.

ValidationCriterion.description: One rubric line for LLM-as-judge validation.

ValidationPolicy.description: Optional gate scoring worker outputs before synthesis.

validator_agent_id.description: Dedicated validator; omitted means the supervisor judges its own workers.

auto_revise.description: Re-run the workers with the validator's feedback when a round fails, up to `max_revision_rounds`. Defaults to true — the server treats only an explicit `false` as off.

selective.description: Re-run only the workers whose output failed, rather than the whole round. Defaults to false.

TeamPolicies.description: Limits and failure handling for a team run.

timeout_ms.description: Total team run timeout. Accepted at any value but only ever RAISED: anything below 3600000 (1 hour) is enforced as 3600000, so that slow local models are not killed mid-run. 0 or absent means uncapped.

on_worker_failure.description: Applied by the auto_dispatch supervisor. Under tool_driven the failure is returned to the supervisor as a tool result instead, and this policy does not run.

max_concurrency.description: Concurrent worker runs in a fan-out (default 8).

TeamSwarmConfig.description: Swarm topology: who starts, and how context travels on handoff.

TeamObjectiveBudget.description: Ceiling for a goal-driven team's pursuit of its objective.

TeamGoalConfig.description: Goal-driven topology: the objective, the review cadence, the budget.

RiskClassification.description: EU AI Act (Article 9) classification for an agent.

assessor.description: Key ID or user ID of whoever classified.

Guardrail.description: A webhook called before or after a run to allow, redact or block it.

ApiKeySummary.description: An API key as listed. The secret is shown once, at creation, and never here.

kind.description: What the key IS: `session` was minted by an OTP/OAuth sign-in and carries a user_id; `api_key` was created deliberately from Settings or the CLI.

LLMProvider.description: An LLM provider the platform knows about, and whether a key is configured.

Program.description: An ordered curriculum an agent delivers.

McpServer.description: An MCP server as returned. `env` and `env_encrypted` are stripped; only the COUNT is disclosed.

assigned_agent_ids.description: Agents allowed to use this server's tools. Absent or empty means no agent sees them — installing a server does not connect it. Set it with PUT /api/v1/agents/{agentId}/mcp-servers, or pass it when installing.

env_count.description: How many env vars are set. The values are never returned.

capabilities.description: Tool names and resource URIs discovered from the server.

McpServerAuth.description: How an http / streamable_http server is authenticated. The secret itself travels in `env` under `env_key` and is encrypted at rest; it is never returned. Query-string placement is not offered: a key in a URL lands in every proxy log on the way.

header.description: Header carrying the secret. Default `Authorization`. Must be an RFC 9110 field name, and may not be one the platform sets itself (`Origin`, `Host`, `Content-Type`, `Accept`).

prefix.description: Value prefix. Defaults to `Bearer ` for `Authorization`, empty for any other header.

env_key.description: Key inside `env` holding the secret. Default `MCP_API_KEY`.

McpTransport.description: `stdio` is blocked in production unless UARP_ALLOW_MCP_STDIO=true.

connect_error.description: Set when the record saved but the session could not be reconnected. This is the only field distinguishing 'saved' from 'saved and working', and it arrives on a 200.

Company.description: Autonomous agent company — strategist + teams pursuing strategic goals.

last_tick_at.description: When the company loop last ATTEMPTED a tick, success or failure. The tick schedule is computed from this (falling back to updated_at while absent), so an ordinary edit no longer postpones the next tick.

last_successful_tick_at.description: When the company loop last completed a tick whose strategist run SUCCEEDED. The `stuck` escalation reads this (falling back to updated_at while absent).

priority.description: UI surface routing; defaults to `info` when omitted.

dedup_key.description: Notifications sharing a dedup_key collapse in the bell with a count badge.

ContentReportInput.description: An abuse/moderation report. Same body shape for the authenticated and anonymous endpoints.

reason.description: Closed vocabulary — unknown values are rejected with 422. `self_harm` raises the resulting operator notification to critical priority.

details.description: Optional free-text note from the reporter.

tenant_id.description: Tenant that owns the reported content — the queue this report lands in.

reporter_fingerprint.description: Truncated SHA-256 of the reporter's IP. Never the raw address; enough to spot one source flooding the queue.

etag.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the content; absent on records written before 2026-09-03 (workspace-store.ts).

Integration.description: OAuth/API integration record (Slack, GitHub, Linear, etc.).

config.description: Connector settings. Secrets are replaced with `<redacted>`.

status.description: `active` is what the server sends for a working integration; the documented `connected` was never emitted.

assigned_agent_ids.description: Agents allowed to use this integration. Present on the live record and read by 7 files in the web; the document omitted it, so a generated client could not tell which agents an integration serves.

embedding_model.description: The embedding model recorded on the base: what the caller sent at create, or the deployment's model; rewritten to the model actually used on every reindex (knowledge-bases.ts:688).

status.description: Deliberately not an enum. The routes write several values for different notions of readiness, and publishing a guessed list is how a client comes to reject a state the server legitimately sends. `ready` is the one observed on a healthy base.

message.description: Plain text rendered on the blocked page; the API does not render HTML. Absent when no message is set — a message that trims to empty is not stored.

enabled_at.description: When the most recent toggle happened.

enabled_by_email.description: Empty string for the synthetic default-off state — that state has no author.

founder_id.description: Empty string when unset — this read never omits the key.

oauth_return_to_hosts.description: Lower-cased hostnames. Empty means nothing is allowlisted.

agent_tenant_id.description: Derived, never sent by a client: set from the caller's tenant when `agent_id` is assigned, so the cron can run the author without a request context.

last_generated_at.description: Drives scheduling. Null until the first successful generation.

slug.description: Derived from the title and unique. Re-minted whenever the title changes.

source.description: Who last shaped it, not who started it — an edit to the title or body of an agent-written post re-stamps this to `manual`.

published_at.description: Null while a draft. Stamped on transition to published and cleared on a return to draft, so a republished post carries a new timestamp rather than its original.

hidden.description: Hides the catalogue row. Presentation only — the runtime still serves the tool. Stored only when true.

status.description: `live` is a one-way latch; closing registration afterwards does not undo it.

completed_at.description: Set once setup first completed. Its presence is what makes the latch one-way.

required_steps.description: The subset that gates going live. Read it rather than hard-coding it.

all_steps.description: Every known step id, required and optional.

missing_required.description: Required steps still outstanding. Non-empty means an attempt to open registration is refused and will name this list.

package_id.description: Lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens, 1-64 characters. Also the map key.

included_specs.description: SPEC refs. Only non-emptiness is checked here; the registry resolver enforces the `@scope/name[@version]` shape at run time, so a malformed ref is accepted by this write and fails later.

stripe_price_id.description: Never returned by the tenant-facing read. Its presence is what protects the package from a silent drop.

updated_at.description: Stamped by the server on every write; not read from the body.

featured.description: True after a POST, false after a DELETE.

state.description: `drift` means it verified once and no longer matches — distinct from `failed`, which never verified.

target.description: What the customer points DNS at. Stored per record so changing the platform target does not silently invalidate domains already pinned to the old one.

last_checked_at.description: Most recent lookup, whatever its result.

verified_at.description: First time it matched. Sticky across verified → drift → verified, so it is not the time of the LAST success.

state.description: `renewal_due` is entered 14 days or less before `not_after`.

issuer_cn.description: Issuer CN, so a CA migration is visible without parsing the leaf.

id.description: Lower-cased. The identity — not settable through the body.

program.description: Pairs the plan with a promo program. Absent when unset.

visibility.description: Omitting this on an update HIDES a previously public plan.

active.description: Omitting this on an update REACTIVATES a deactivated plan. Send it explicitly on every write.

owner_tenant_id.description: The tenant that earns the reward.

subscriber_bonus_tokens.description: Welcome grant to the redeeming tenant. Absent when unset.

target_plan_id.description: Scopes the code to ONE plan: the reward is skipped when it is set and does not match the plan being paid for. Absent means the code pays out on every plan.

uses.description: Server-maintained; carried across a replacing write.

target_plan_id.description: Resend this on every update — the write replaces, so omitting it unscopes the code.

active.description: Omitting this on an update REACTIVATES a deactivated code.

mef_config.description: What an operator stored. Null when nothing is overridden — never an empty object.

effective.description: What the runtime will do. All false when the mission service is absent platform-wide, whatever the overrides say.

TenantQuotaOverrides.description: Per-tenant overrides applied on top of the plan's quotas. Partial by nature: only the keys actually overridden are present.

TenantSocialLinks.description:
REPLACES the stored object; it is not merged. A PATCH carrying one platform leaves the tenant with that one platform and nothing else, so read-modify-write is the only safe shape — send every link you want to keep, `custom` included.

Values are filtered, not rejected: a URL that does not match `^https?://.{3,500}$` is dropped and the request still answers 200. Nothing is hidden by this — the response body carries the tenant as STORED, so the saved `social_links` is in the answer and a second GET is not needed to see what survived. Compare what you sent against what came back; a key missing from the answer was refused.

Length is applied BEFORE the pattern, which matters: a url longer than 500 characters is CUT to 500 and then matches, so it is stored TRUNCATED rather than refused — a different link that still looks like one. Compare lengths too, not just presence. `custom` takes at most 5 entries, each with a label and a url; labels are stripped of angle brackets and cut to 50, urls to 500, on the same before-validation order. Documented 2026-09-17 after the web lane measured the filtering and could not find it described anywhere.

plan_id.description: Resolved plan id — present on the normal answer, absent on the bootstrap branch.

IntegrationCatalogItem.description: Available integration (connector) type in the catalog

id.description: Connector id (e.g. github, stripe, notion, slack)

oauth_provider.description: Present when the connector authorises through another connector's OAuth provider (google_calendar, gmail, google_drive and google_sheets all say `google`). A client builds the authorize URL from this when set, from `id` otherwise. Absent for every other connector.

required_oauth_scopes.description: The OAuth scopes the connector needs, so a client can show them BEFORE the visitor clicks Connect rather than leaving the IdP consent screen to be the first place they are seen. Absent — not empty — for api_key connectors and for OAuth connectors that declare none.

OAuthCompleteRequest.description: Body to complete OAuth after callback

AuthVerifyCodeRequest.description: Body for POST /api/v1/auth/verify-code. No request_id; code is bound to email only.

code.description: OTP from email (6 digits); spaces are stripped server-side

AuthVerifyCodeResponse.description: Success response: API key to use as Bearer token

api_key.description: uarp_<prefix>_<secret>; store and use as Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

OAuthLoginProviderItem.description: Public-safe descriptor for an OAuth login (identity) provider. Surfaces only what the login page needs to decide which buttons to render — never exposes client_secret.

enabled.description: true when the operator has configured client_id+client_secret AND set enabled=true. False values mean clicking the button would 404.

OAuthLoginProviderConfigStatus.description: Admin view of one provider's current config. client_secret is never echoed; client_secret_hint shows the last 4 chars so the operator can confirm storage.

configured.description: false when no record exists yet; remaining fields are absent in that case

client_secret_hint.description: Masked tail of the stored secret (e.g. "••••a1b2"). null if no secret on file.

scopes.description: null when no override; provider defaults apply

OAuthLoginProviderConfigUpdate.description: Body for PUT /api/v1/admin/oauth-login-providers/{provider}. Merges with existing record: an operator flipping `enabled` or rotating `scopes` does not need to re-paste the secret. The first-time PUT (no existing record) requires both client_id and client_secret.

client_id.description: OAuth app client ID issued by the provider

client_secret.description: OAuth app client secret. Stored verbatim in admin KV; never echoed back.

enabled.description: Defaults to existing value, or true on first write if omitted

scopes.description: Optional override of the provider's default scope list. Omit to inherit defaults.

OAuthLoginProviderConfigUpdateResponse.description: Result after PUT — confirms the persisted state

OAuthLoginProviderConfigDeleted.description: Result after DELETE — record removed from admin KV

configured.description: Always false after a successful DELETE

MissionMetrics.description: Aggregated spend for the whole mission. Written on the terminal transition, so it is absent while the mission is still running.

retries.description: Objective retries across the mission — a strike counter, not an HTTP retry count.

Mission.description: A Mission Execution Framework run: a goal decomposed into objectives, executed under an authorization gate with checkpoints and an after-action review. Sent by every mission endpoint that answers with the record itself.

session_id.description: Chat session the mission was started from.

created_by.description: User id, or an agent id when a sub-mission was spawned by an agent.

classification.description: Why MEF took the request. `quick_reply` never reaches execution.

objective_ids.description: Root objective ids in plan order.

checkpoint_ids.description: Appended chronologically as objectives verify; a resume replays from the last one.

aar_id.description: Set once the after-action review is finalized — see GET /missions/{missionId}/aar.

outcome.description: Terminal outcome. `partial` means some objectives verified and some did not.

failed_objective_ids.description: Subset of objective_ids that failed verification.

deadline.description: ISO 8601 hard deadline the runtime enforces against.

started_at.description: Set when the status first leaves `draft`.

completed_at.description: Set when the status becomes terminal.

ObjectiveBudget.description: Per-objective ceiling and what has been spent against it. The executor stops an objective that would cross a max.

ObjectiveRoE.description: Rules of engagement: what the objective may do alone, what needs a human, and what it must never do.

ObjectiveDecisionPoint.description: A branch in the plan: when `condition` holds, execution continues at the matching branch's objective instead of the next one in order.

Objective.description: One unit of mission work. Sent in full by GET /missions/{missionId}/objectives and by the PATCH that edits one.

parent_id.description: Parent objective, or null for a root objective of the mission.

success_criteria.description: What the verifier checks before the objective counts as done.

status.description: Lifecycle, owned by the executor — PATCH cannot set it.

assigned_agent_id.description: Agent that executes this objective. Mutually exclusive with assigned_team_id in practice.

dependencies.description: Objective ids that must verify first. The plan is a DAG.

commanders_intent.description: The end state to preserve when the literal instruction stops fitting.

final_status.description: The objective's status when the mission ended.

strikes_used.description: Retries spent on this objective before it settled.

verified.description: Whether the success criteria were checked and held.

AARLesson.description: A pattern seen in this mission and what to do about it next time.

AAR.description: After-action review, built once when the mission reaches a terminal status. `failure_analysis` is present only when something failed.

PlannedObjective.description: An objective as supplied in a caller-written plan. Dependencies are INDICES into `objectives`, because ids do not exist until the plan is persisted.

depends_on_indices.description: Indices into `objectives`; must form a DAG or the plan is rejected.

budget.description: Ceilings only — the spent_* counters are created by the server.

PlannedMission.description: A fully decomposed plan. Supplying one skips the LLM planner entirely.

requires_authorization.description: When true the mission stops at `awaiting_authorization` instead of executing — the gate for destructive or externally visible plans.

MissionStartResponse.description: What POST /missions answers. `plan` is echoed back only when the server planned the mission from a goal.

objective_ids.description: Persisted objective ids, in plan order.

classification.description: The intake decision. A `quick_reply` mission is recorded but is not mission work.

TenantOverview.description: The single aggregate behind Mission Control: fleet, run buckets, approvals, quota, worker health and schedule risk in one call instead of N.

by_execution_mode.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (no such field on v2's record); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

bridge.description: Optional: absent on a server without the bridge concept (v2 has none); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

head_agent_id.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (no such field on v2's record); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

top_by_cost.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (v2 measures no cost, tokens or system health); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

last_run_at.description: Agent id → the timestamp of its most recent run in the scanned window.

active_count.description: Queued, running, paused, awaiting approval or awaiting input.

cost_24h_usd.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (v2 measures no cost, tokens or system health); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

execution_mode.description: Passed through from the run record. Absent for platform-dispatched cloud runs; `bridge` is the only value the platform writes (run-dispatch.ts, bridge.ts); `async` only echoes what a client supplied at run creation and has never been stored on production (measured 2026-09-10 over 8605 run records: absent 7738, bridge 867, async 0).

scanned.description: How many run records the aggregate actually looked at. The scan is capped, so a busy tenant's numbers describe the scanned window, not all history.

usage.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (v2 measures no cost, tokens or system health); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

cost.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (v2 measures no cost, tokens or system health); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

system.description: Optional: absent when the server does not track it (v2 measures no cost, tokens or system health); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

healthy.description: False when no cron job is registered — the signal that scheduled work has stopped.

at_risk.description: Paused, errored, or carrying consecutive failures — a silently dead cron. Optional: absent when the server does not track it (no such field on v2's record); clients must tolerate absence. v1 serves it.

InboxItem.description: One run waiting on a person, with what it is actually asking rather than just its status.

summary.description: One line: the tool being requested, the question, or the error.

detail.description: Longer body — tool arguments, error detail, question context. Empty string when there is none.

options.description: The agent's own choices, for `input` items. Empty otherwise.

TenantInbox.description: The “what needs a human” queue. The overview answers how many; this answers which, and what they are asking.

counts.description: Counted over the whole scan, NOT over `items` — so `limit` truncating the list does not move them. The SCAN is capped too, though, and that cap they cannot see past: when `truncated` is true these are a floor, not a total.

scanned.description: Run records inspected; the scan is capped.

truncated.description: The scan hit its cap, so `counts` is a floor rather than a total. `scanned` alone cannot tell you this — the number only means something to a caller who already knows what the cap is.

PublicChatAnalytics.description: Funnel for public (unauthenticated) chat surfaces: visits, engagement, messages, with the usual breakdowns.

conversion.description: Ratios, not percentages: 0.25 means a quarter.

PlatformEconomics.description: Platform profit and loss: Stripe revenue against real host spend and the LLM provider bill. Super-admin only. Served from a short-lived cache — `cache` says which.

stripe_configured.description: False on a deployment with no Stripe key; the figures are then zeros, not an error.

error.description: Present when Stripe could not be reached; the rest of the payload is still served.

month_to_date_usd.description: Real accrued spend from the provider's own meter.

monthly_run_rate_usd.description: Sum of droplet list prices — steady state, not accrued.

llm.description: What the platform paid model providers for tokens, from the usage shards' pre-markup `provider_cost` summed over every tenant. The largest variable cost; absent from this report until 2026-09-02.

period.description: YYYY-MM, UTC — the period the usage shards are keyed by.

month_to_date_billed_usd.description: What tenants were billed for the same usage (provider × markup).

run_rate_basis.description: `previous_period` — last month's full bill; `month_to_date_extrapolated` — this month's spend scaled to a full month, a guess that is loudest on the 1st; `none` — nothing recorded yet.

caveats.description: What the number does not know: own-key proxy traffic is counted although the tenant paid it; shards older than the field count 0.

monthly_llm_usd.description: `llm.monthly_run_rate_usd` — see `llm.run_rate_basis` for how it was reached.

monthly_margin_usd.description: MRR − infra run rate − LLM run rate.

margin_percent.description: Null when there is no revenue to divide by — not zero, which would read as a 0% margin.

cache.description: `hit` — served from cache; `miss` — computed and cached; `bypass` — recomputed because `refresh=1`.

ProjectGrant.description: One person's access to a private project.

access.description: `view` opens the chats and the brief; `edit` also rewrites them.

Project.description: A named body of work that chats belong to: standing instructions, the knowledge bases its chats may search, and the files they can read. An agent is *who* answers; a project is *what about*.

instructions.description: Injected into the system prompt below the agent's own prompt and above personal preferences.

file_ids.description: Ids that no longer resolve to a file in this tenant are dropped on write — an attachment that lies is worse than a rejected one.

visibility.description: `tenant` (the default, and what every pre-existing project is) or `private`.

archived_at.description: Absent or null when the project is live. Archiving hides it from the default list and loses nothing.

sessions.description: The chats filed under this project, most recently updated first.

access.description: What THIS caller may do. `none` never reaches a client — it is answered as 404.

ProjectDetail.description: A project with its chats and the caller's own access level.

UserPreferences.description: Personal instructions that apply to every conversation this person has, whichever agent answers.

enabled.description: Off keeps the text but stops it reaching any run — the switch people actually want when an instruction misfires.

max_chars.description: Server-enforced ceiling for `custom_instructions`. Sent on every response so a client does not hard-code it.

agent_name.description: Resolved for display; absent if the agent record is gone.

status.description: `paused` or `error`, or accumulated failures, is what a “silently dead cron” looks like.

AccountExport.description: The JSON form of an account export. The same bundle the zip contains, as one document.

complete.description: False when a size ceiling was hit; `omitted` then says what was left out. An export that quietly drops things is worse than one that admits it.

files.description: Path inside the bundle → its contents (`account.json`, `projects.md`, `memory.md`, `chats/…`).

NotificationTarget.description: Where outbound notifications go. **Secrets never leave the server**: a webhook's signing secret is reported only as `has_signing_secret`, a device token only by its last four characters, and a Web Push endpoint only by host — the path carries a subscription identifier.

enabled.description: A disabled target is kept for audit and skipped at fan-out.

last_delivered_at.description: Last success — the field that tells a dead webhook from a quiet one.

has_signing_secret.description: Whether a secret is configured. The secret itself is never returned.

device_token_suffix.description: Last four characters of the device token, for visual identification only.

endpoint_host.description: Host only — `(invalid endpoint)` when the stored URL will not parse.

SpecToolCatalog.description: Which SPEC output view renders each tool's result, for the builder UI. Keyed by tool name; the first view claiming a tool wins, and a view whose JSON will not parse is skipped rather than failing the call.

drawings.description: The canvases this agent's SPECs put their output on (docs/DESIGNER-CANVAS.md §5.1) — today only `drawing`. Always present: empty means no drawing canvas, absence means an older server, and a client must not confuse the two.

tools.description: Tool name → the SPEC that owns it and the view to render its output with. Integration aliases map onto their base tool's view.

output_view.description: The parsed view document, or null when the stored view was unparseable.

PlatformInfo.description: What an unauthenticated page may know about this deployment. Deliberately minimal — no secrets and no wizard step names, so a probe cannot enumerate what setup still has pending.

public_base_url.description: The platform's own base URL, so a client need not bake it into its bundle.

contact_emails.description: Role → address. Always an object, possibly empty — a client gates each link on presence rather than handling nulls.

setup_complete.description: True once the platform is live.

MaintenanceStatus.description: Whether the platform is closed for maintenance. Unauthenticated: a client that cannot sign in still needs to know why. `message` is plain text and is never rendered as HTML by the API.

message.description: Absent when no message was set.

LandingOverrides.description: Operator-set text and partner logos for the public landing page.

texts.description: Override key → text. Empty when nothing is overridden.

partners.description: Null means never configured, which a client may render differently from an empty list.

version.description: KV versionstamp of the stored record. The admin form sends it back on write so two operators cannot silently overwrite each other.

FleetLayoutUpdate.description: What a client SENDS when saving the canvas. The stored record additionally carries `updated_at`, and the response may carry `dropped` — both are produced by the server, so neither belongs in a request.

positions.description: Agent id → its place on the canvas.

FleetLayout.description: The operator's canvas: where each agent sits, how they are wired, and the notes and not-yet-real nodes drawn around them. Persisted as one record per tenant.

positions.description: Agent id → its place on the canvas.

type.description: Edge kind; a workflow edge is what makes the graph runnable.

frame.description: A frame is a large titled rectangle drawn BEHIND the nodes to group a squad.

kind.description: memory / knowledge / tool / condition / … — a node the operator drew that is not a backend entity yet.

dropped.description: Present ONLY when the save discarded something. Counts per collection of the items that did not survive the caps or validation. A 200 without this field saved everything.
